comparison: Both strongly support model validation (C31-C38). OpenEval emphasizes specific validation metrics (correlation, independent parameterization, external validation), while peer reviewers praise 'exceptional' execution and note prior concerns were addressed. High agreement on model accuracy.

Both support computational methodology and dataset scale (C39-C40, C136-C137). OpenEval focuses on convergence testing and statistical power, while peer reviewers praise the 'exceptional' large-scale design and 'robust dataset.' Strong agreement on methodological rigor.

Both strongly support existence and properties of scaling laws (C4-C6, C47, C131, C168). OpenEval emphasizes consistency across PLDs and predictive capability, while peer reviewers affirm 'predictive scaling laws' and 'reasonable and insightful' results. Complete agreement on core findings.

Both support aromatic substitution effects (C41, C52-C53, C55, C57). OpenEval provides detailed quantitative characterization of linear scaling and mechanistic interpretation, while peer reviewers accept findings as part of 'linear dependence on substitutions.' Full agreement.

Both support aromatic deletion effects with √L dependence (C42, C59, C62-C67, C139, C141-C142). OpenEval details mechanistic explanation involving network disruption and valency, while peer reviewers affirm 'nuanced, clear, and well-motivated' interpretations. Complete agreement on length-dependent scaling.

Both support Arg deletion scaling with 1/L dependence (C43-C44, C76-C80, C144, C146, C148-C149). OpenEval emphasizes distinct scaling from aromatics and mechanistic basis, while peer reviewers accept arginine as key sticker residue. OpenEval R6 excludes C83 (Arg→Lys), which peer R6 includes.

OpenEval R7 addresses Arg→Lys substitution effects (C83-C86, C153-C156) with twofold difference quantification. Peer R6 includes C83 and related claims (C151-C156) as part of broader arginine findings. Both support the results, though grouped differently.

Both support polar residue effects (C45, C95-C96, C98-C99, C162). OpenEval notes modest magnitude and speculative mechanism based on dipole moments, while peer reviewers accept findings as part of overall 'reasonable and insightful' results. Agreement on subtle effects.

OpenEval R9 addresses neutral residue mutations (C102, C104-C119, C157-C160) with detailed quantitative predictions. Peer R7 includes some overlapping claims (C157-C160) as part of polar/spacer residue findings. Both support the subtle effects observed.

OpenEval R9 includes convergence testing and emergent behavior (C106, C117-C118). Peer R8 specifically praises 'pedagogical nature' of convergence discussion (C51) and accepts emergent collective behavior. Strong agreement on methodological transparency.

Both support sequence patterning effects using σ_aro parameter (C120-C121, C123, C125). OpenEval emphasizes inverse correlation and mechanistic explanation, while peer reviewers accept as supporting finding consistent with prior work. Complete agreement.

Both acknowledge model limitations (C126-C129, C93-C94, C166-C167). OpenEval treats as appropriate caveats defining scope, while peer reviewers note authors 'carefully acknowledge these limitations' and don't see them as major weaknesses. Agreement on transparent limitation reporting.

Both address model's handling of polarity (C50, C93-C94, C166-C167). OpenEval supports implicit incorporation approach as reasonable, while peer reviewers accept this as acknowledged limitation. Agreement that approach is suitable despite constraints.

Both express uncertainty about forward-looking applications (C7, C46, C132-C134, C169, C171). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN requiring future validation, while peer reviewers note these are speculative claims not directly validated. Strong agreement on need for future demonstration.

OpenEval R11 supports compositional characteristics of PLD family (C49, C69-C70) based on Figure 1B analysis. No corresponding peer review evaluation explicitly addresses these compositional claims, though they underpin the family-based analysis approach.

OpenEval R13 supports extensive background and context claims (C1-C2, C8-C30, C48, C68, C71-C72, C87-C92, C100) as well-established by literature. Peer reviewers do not explicitly evaluate these background claims, focusing instead on novel findings.

OpenEval R16 supports computational method capabilities (C135) with citations and validation results. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate this claim about current computational methods, though it's implicit in their acceptance of the approach.
Minor overlap: OpenEval R2 includes C3 (computational methodology), which peer R1 includes as part of model validation context. Both support the claim but group it differently with related findings.
